arguments.name: procedure
arguments.blurb: The procedure this config object is used for

arguments.name: run-mode
arguments.blurb: The run mode

arguments.name: image
arguments.blurb: The input image

arguments.name: drawables
arguments.blurb: The input drawables

arguments.name: align-threshold
arguments.blurb: If two endpoints are closer than this, they are made to be equal.

arguments.name: corner-always-threshold
arguments.blurb: If the angle defined by a point and its predecessors and successors is smaller than this, it's a corner, even if it's within 'corner_surround' pixels of a point with a smaller angle.

arguments.name: corner-surround
arguments.blurb: Number of points to consider when determining if a point is a corner or not.

arguments.name: corner-threshold
arguments.blurb: If a point, its predecessors, and its successors define an angle smaller than this, it's a corner.

arguments.name: error-threshold
arguments.blurb: Amount of error at which a fitted spline is unacceptable. If any pixel is further away than this from the fitted curve, we try again.

arguments.name: filter-alternative-surround
arguments.blurb: A second number of adjacent points to consider when filtering.

arguments.name: filter-epsilon
arguments.blurb: If the angles between the vectors produced by filter_surround and filter_alternative_surround points differ by more than this, use the one from filter_alternative_surround.

arguments.name: filter-iteration-count
arguments.blurb: Number of times to smooth original data points.  Increasing this number dramatically --- to 50 or so --- can produce vastly better results. But if any points that 'should' be corners aren't found, the curve goes to hell around that point.

arguments.name: filter-percent
arguments.blurb: To produce the new point, use the old point plus this times the neighbors.

arguments.name: filter-secondary-surround
arguments.blurb: Number of adjacent points to consider if 'filter_surround' points defines a straight line.

arguments.name: filter-surround
arguments.blurb: Number of adjacent points to consider when filtering.

arguments.name: keep-knees
arguments.blurb: Says whether or not to remove 'knee' points after finding the outline.

arguments.name: line-reversion-threshold
arguments.blurb: If a spline is closer to a straight line than this, it remains a straight line, even if it would otherwise be changed back to a curve. This is weighted by the square of the curve length, to make shorter curves more likely to be reverted.

arguments.name: line-threshold
arguments.blurb: How many pixels (on the average) a spline can diverge from the line determined by its endpoints before it is changed to a straight line.

arguments.name: reparametrize-improvement
arguments.blurb: If reparameterization doesn't improve the fit by this much percent, stop doing it. Amount of error at which it is pointless to reparameterize.

arguments.name: reparametrize-threshold
arguments.blurb: Amount of error at which it is pointless to reparameterize.  This happens, for example, when we are trying to fit the outline of the outside of an 'O' with a single spline. The initial fit is not good enough for the Newton-Raphson iteration to improve it.  It may be that it would be better to detect the cases where we didn't find any corners.

arguments.name: subdivide-search
arguments.blurb: Percentage of the curve away from the worst point to look for a better place to subdivide.

arguments.name: subdivide-surround
arguments.blurb: Number of points to consider when deciding whether a given point is a better place to subdivide.

arguments.name: subdivide-threshold
arguments.blurb: How many pixels a point can diverge from a straight line and still be considered a better place to subdivide.

arguments.name: tangent-surround
arguments.blurb: Number of points to look at on either side of a point when computing the approximation to the tangent at that point.
